solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: She's not entirely above the law

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so a woman's name sits inside the words that follow, spanning them

explanation.surface: A woman who thinks herself not quite exempt from legal rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely above the law' reads as a comment on her ethics; it says the name is tucked inside 'above the law'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel is a female first name, so a woman can be referred to by the pronoun given.

clue.text: Yours truly lifted head to carve

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the word is raised up the column, read bottom to top

parts.note: the setter referring to themselves, giving the pronoun ME
a boss is the head of an organisation

explanation.surface: The writer raised a leader's figure in order to sculpt it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yours truly' is the setter, ME; 'lifted' turns it to EM in this down entry, followed by BOSS.
explanation.definitionFit: To emboss is to carve or mould a raised design into a surface.

clue.text: Party raising the temperature in Parliament?

parts.note: the House is either chamber of Parliament, such as the House of Commons
making things hotter is warming

explanation.surface: A political party stirring up heated debate in the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as WARMING in the HOUSE, the phrase is put in answer order: HOUSE first, then WARMING.
explanation.definitionFit: A housewarming is a celebration held when someone moves into a new home.

clue.text: Heather Lake's bra and pants?

parts.note: ling is another name for common heather
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: Underwear belonging to a woman called Heather Lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather Lake' poses as someone's name; it is two plain pieces, the plant LING and Lake ERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear, of which a bra and pants are examples, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Old primate, a quiet celebrity on the up

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

indicators.note: in a down clue, on the up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a celebrity is a big name

explanation.surface: An ancient ape who is a quiet celebrity whose fame is growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old primate' points to the extinct hominid, not an elderly ape; P is the musical marking piano.
explanation.definitionFit: An early hominid ancestor of humans is popularly called this, an extinct primate.

clue.text: State of S English county appalling at first

parts.note: the Isle of Wight, abbreviated IOW, is a county off the south coast of England

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: The condition of a southern English county is appalling at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like 'condition' in the surface; it is a US state. The Isle of Wight is an island county off southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Buzz monsieur to go with us for a dip

parts.note: a buzz is a low hum
M. is the standard abbreviation for the French title monsieur

explanation.surface: Phone a Frenchman to come along with us for a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dip' suggests a swim, but it is the food sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Hummus is a chickpea paste served as a dip with bread or vegetables.

clue.text: I have arrived dead on time? You, one hears, unprepared

parts.note: announcing 'I have arrived' is saying I'm here, giving I'M
someone exactly on time is prompt

indicators.note: says the word before is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of arriving exactly on time, then notes the listener is caught unready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one hears' applies only to 'You', which sounds like the letter U.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impromptu is done without rehearsal or preparation, off the cuff.

clue.text: Champions, excited, wire reps in NZ

indicators.note: agitated, stirred up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Winning sportspeople, thrilled, send a message to agents in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wire' looks like a verb, to send a telegram, but its letters are fodder with REPS IN NZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Champions are those who have won, and those who take a prize are winners of it.

clue.text: Bear the onset of bankruptcy before downfall

indicators.note: the onset is the beginning, so only the first letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: a downfall is a person's ruin

explanation.surface: Endure the start of insolvency before total collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like a verb, to endure, but it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruin is a traditional folk name for a bear, from the Dutch for brown.

clue.text: My amusing exercises here?

indicators.note: putting through their paces works the letters around into a new order

explanation.surface: A wry remark about where someone's comical workouts take place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercises' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal; the whole clue also describes the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A gym, the place where people do physical exercise, is this in full.

clue.text: Use a needle having three points?

parts.note: south, east and west are three points of the compass, whose abbreviations are S, E and W
east, the second compass point, abbreviated E
west, the third compass point, abbreviated W

explanation.surface: A sewing needle is said to have three sharp points.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'points' are compass points, not needle tips; the question mark flags the letters run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitching with thread is done by passing a needle through fabric, and three compass letters spell it.

clue.text: Assigns new labels to right food additives

parts.note: E numbers are the EU codes given to approved food additives

explanation.surface: Someone relabels the correct food additives on a list.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving items fresh numbers is giving them new identifying labels.

clue.text: Undid gym pants getting dirty

indicators.note: British slang for rubbish or poor, so the letters are in a bad state and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone loosened their gym trousers, which were becoming grubby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers but is British slang for rubbish, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Muddying something is making it soiled with mud, so it is becoming unclean.

clue.text: Insult by English copper journalist grilled

parts.note: a barb is a cutting, insulting remark
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
ED, an editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter was abused by an English policeman and then questioned hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman and 'grilled' like interrogated; one is the metal, the other is cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbecued food is cooked over an open flame, in the same way as grilled food.

clue.text: He turns up in tie, late

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the other piece

parts.note: to tie is to bind

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A man arrives wearing a tie but is overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' looks like arriving; it reverses HE to EH, which goes 'in' BIND.
explanation.definitionFit: Being behind schedule or behind with payments is being late or in arrears.

clue.text: Completely remove our pot that's broken

indicators.note: a smashed pot ends up in pieces, so the letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener takes out a plant whose pot has cracked.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull something out by the roots is to get rid of it entirely.

clue.text: Diamonds one found next to church

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A diamond found lying beside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found next to' just joins I and CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is slang for diamonds, from their cold glitter.

clue.text: Sweetheart hypothetically, in part, crude

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An imagined lover described as somewhat vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and down to earth, much as crude humour is.

clue.text: Pay Harris for repairs: I can fix locks

indicators.note: something sent for repairs gets taken apart and put back together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A locksmith asks to be paid for fixing locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' are hair, not door fastenings.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair spray is a lacquer that holds a hairstyle in place, so it keeps one's tresses set.

clue.text: Stuff son consumed

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies
consumed food is ate it

explanation.definitionFit: To fill someone to repletion with food is to satisfy their appetite fully.

clue.text: Bungling in record time

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone making a mess of an attempt at a record time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record time' reads as a fast finish; it is EP and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungling person is clumsy and incompetent, lacking skill.

clue.text: Unusual thing: good to have this for one's retirement?

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: An odd object would be nice to own for when one stops working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' scrambles THING to NIGHT. 'retirement' means going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is worn when one goes to bed, retiring for the night.

clue.text: Fellow crossing street blowing hard

indicators.note: one piece goes across the other, holding it inside

parts.note: a guy is a fellow, a man

explanation.surface: A man crossing a road, puffing and panting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing hard' looks like a person out of breath; it describes the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusty weather has strong sudden bursts of wind.
